source_snapshot.script: Private account-delete; 5 attended and 5 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; requires an operator-provided numeric ACC_ID and post-GET, but lacks exact username/object mapping, admin/current-session protection, recovery access and session invalidation.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; inventory and resolve one approved temporary/non-admin account URI, keep an independent admin session, explicitly approve one DELETE, prove absence/session revocation and never infer or auto-recreate identity.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly treats DELETE as state-changing, but a numeric ID alone is not identity proof and its generic restore suggestion could create a different security object.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly makes exact object mapping and recovery-admin continuity prerequisites and rejects automatic recreation.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A Redfish account URI may be keyed by numeric member ID even when the source describes `{Username}`. The deletion target must be resolved by reading the member object and matching username, role, enabled state and owner approval; path text alone is never sufficient.

original_test_intent: Verify that one explicitly approved temporary, non-recovery BMC account can be deleted through its exact Redfish object and becomes unusable while all unrelated accounts and an independent administrator remain intact.
original_method: Export a redacted account/member inventory, resolve the approved username to one exact object URI, prove it is not the active or recovery administrator, validate session-revocation semantics, obtain immediate approval, issue one protected DELETE, verify object absence and failed authentication/session invalidation, compare final inventory to baseline, and preserve audit evidence.
manual_activity: The BMC security owner selects and approves the exact disposable account object, confirms it is not required for administration or recovery, observes deletion and verifies the independent administrator remains usable.
required_inputs: Vendor AccountService member and DELETE semantics
Proof target is temporary and non-recovery
safety_requirements: Never infer account identity from URI number or username text alone
Never expose secrets in URLs, history or evidence
Do not use unapproved TLS bypass
Compare unrelated accounts before and after
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and export redacted inventory
Resolve exact account object and attributes
Verify object absence, auth rejection and session invalidation
Compare final inventory and archive evidence without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact target identity and deletion
Review ambiguous completion or unexpected inventory change
Direct vendor recovery if deletion was wrong

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A DELETE of the exact member URI is the correct operation, but an operator-supplied numeric ACC_ID without object-attribute reconciliation can select the wrong security principal and its post-GET is incomplete.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate AccountService members, resolve one owner-approved temporary username to a unique object URI and verify role/status, then issue one protected DELETE and prove absence, session invalidation, authentication rejection and recovery-admin continuity.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The single-account delete intent and 5/5-minute estimate remain; credential-in-URL, generic clearing, inferred ID and automatic restore are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed deletion manifest containing target URI, username, role/status, baseline inventory hash, approval and recovery-admin identity; link it to DELETE and all post-state checks.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds semantic target proof, session effects and unrelated-account integrity around an ambiguous path placeholder.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An HTTP response or missing object alone cannot prove the intended principal was deleted, its sessions were revoked or recovery access survived.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Deletion may be irreversible for the original identity and policy metadata. Recreating the same username is not rollback and is outside this case.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define whether AccountService members are keyed by numeric ID, username or another identifier and how active sessions are invalidated. The source `{Username}` placeholder must be resolved from live member data, never converted by guesswork.
expected_evidence: Target/AccountService identity and hashed redacted baseline inventory
Exact approved URI-to-username/role/status mapping and recovery-admin proof
Vendor delete/session contract and explicit approval
Trusted TLS/auth/client metadata with secrets redacted
Complete DELETE response and exactly-one-command audit
Object absence, authentication rejection, session invalidation, final inventory integrity and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, DELETE procedure and criterion consistently require removal of one account. The `{Username}` versus possible numeric member URI and root-resource GET are incomplete target/verification details rather than competing objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The exact member mapping, recovery administrator and delete/session semantics are obtainable inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if the target cannot be made unique or recovery access cannot be protected.

review_improvement: Prevents deletion by guessed ID, protects the current/recovery administrator and proves both principal and session removal without inventing rollback.
independent_technical_reasoning: Account deletion changes identity, authorization and session state. Safe targeting requires matching the live object URI to stable attributes and owner intent, while successful cleanup requires both collection absence and invalidated credentials/tokens. Recovery-admin continuity is an independent invariant because a correctly deleted wrong account is still a critical failure.
